en-US.author: Dennis Park
en-US.description: A multi-platform GUI SSH terminal with a files panel, a built-in editor and split panes.
en-US.longDescription:
rulogman is a desktop SSH client written in Rust and drawn with gpui, the
GPU-accelerated UI framework behind the Zed editor. Connections are saved as
profiles — host, user, password or private key — and open in tabs that can be split
into panes, each with its own connection and its own scrollback. The terminal itself
is alacritty_terminal, so colors, cursor addressing, the alternate screen and
full-screen programs such as vim, tmux and htop behave as they do in any other
terminal.

Beside the terminal sits a files panel that browses the session's filesystem over
SFTP on a channel of the same connection, with drag-and-drop transfers and a
breadcrumb path. Right-clicking a file opens it in a built-in editor tab with line
numbers, find and replace, undo and syntax highlighting for seventeen formats, and
Ctrl+S writes it back over the connection it came from. Port forwarding rules,
including a SOCKS proxy, are saved with the profile and open as soon as the shell is
up, and profiles can be imported from the OpenSSH client's config file.

Not every terminal is remote: local shells are first-class too, with PowerShell, cmd
and every installed WSL distribution offered from the start screen. Host keys are
checked on the trust-on-first-use convention, and passwords and key passphrases go
to the Windows Credential Manager rather than to any configuration file. Themes and
terminal color schemes are picked independently, scheme files use Windows
Terminal's format, and the interface is available in eight languages.
en-US.name: rulogman
en-US.releaseNotes:
rulogman 0.6.6 — idle Windows and WSL shells that close without asking, saves on a NAS whose SFTP view differs from its shell, a comment toggle that keeps the selection, and rugpui 0.1.17.
- Idle Windows and WSL shells close without asking. Closing a window asked first for every local shell on Windows, even one that had run nothing: a console has no foreground process group, and every Windows shell is started from a command line, which the close guard took for -e. cmd and PowerShell now count as idle when they have no child process and have drawn their prompt again since the last command line, which also catches a script or cmdlet running inside PowerShell itself. A WSL shell is read inside its distribution, like a remote one, and is idle while its terminal's foreground group is its own.
- Remote files save on a NAS whose SFTP view differs from its shell. A NAS such as Synology serves SFTP from a view of its own (/home, /photo, /usbshare1) while its shell sees /volume1/homes/<user>, /volume1/photo and /volumeUSB1/usbshare, so opening a file worked and saving it failed. A save now creates its staging directory over SFTP and asks the shell which directory holds it, and a root save matches the file by its opened bytes when the SFTP path does not exist in the shell.
- The comment toggle in the editor keeps the selection. The same lines stay selected, a backwards selection stays backwards, and the caret stays beside the character it was next to, instead of collapsing to a caret at the old offset.
- Shift+Backspace deletes backwards in editors and text fields, as Backspace does. It was bound to nothing and reached the text only through whatever the input method made of it.
- Shared libraries are updated to rugpui 0.1.17, and russh to 0.65 for RUSTSEC-2026-0492 and RUSTSEC-2026-0495. UI dependencies and framework patches are pinned to rugpui's published release commit.

Requirements
- Linux: glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and later, or a distribution built on them, MX Linux 23 among them.
